resources.name: SoundBetter
resources.description: Music production marketplace with 50,000+ vetted music professionals across 176 countries. Find session musicians, producers, singers, and engineers by reviews, price, location, and credits. Acquired by Spotify; now operates with a storefront/subscription model for professionals.
resources.cost: Free to post jobs and hire; clients pay no platform fee. Professionals pay $9.99/mo or $99/yr for a custom storefront with 10% commission on sales. Commission-based pricing also available for service gigs.
highlights: Storefront model for pros to sell sounds and skills

resources.name: AirGigs
resources.description: Marketplace for hiring session musicians, vocalists, and audio engineers for remote recording. Launched in 2012, it features detailed artist profiles, audio samples, and secure escrow payments. Recently updated pricing structure.
resources.cost: Free to browse. One-time $20 activation fee for sellers. Buyers pay 4.7% service fee ($5 minimum). Sellers pay 10% commission (featured) or 15% (non-featured), with $8 minimum commission per order.
highlights: Local-based job posts available ($30/listing with social promotion)

resources.name: Fiverr — Music & Audio
resources.description: Global freelance marketplace with a large Music & Audio category. Find session guitarists, drummers, bassists, vocalists, and more. Filter by instrument, genre, budget, and delivery time.
resources.cost: Services start at ~$5, though session work typically ranges $20–$120+. Buyer fees: 5.5% + $2 on orders under $50 (fees vary; verify current schedule on Fiverr).

resources.name: Musiversal
resources.description: Subscription-based platform for live, directed recording sessions with world-class musicians. Collaborate in real time, give feedback instantly, and receive takes within 15 minutes.
resources.cost: Unlimited membership $249/mo (cancel or pause anytime); new members join via a monthly waitlist. Full Mix add-on: $249/session. Quick Mix (35–45 min) included in membership.
highlights: All instruments: drums, guitar, bass, keys, strings, horns, vocals
Tracks made on it include a Latin Grammy winner

resources.name: Supreme Tracks
resources.description: Curated roster of professional session musicians (200+ from New York, Nashville, LA, Europe) who record in pro studios. A session producer reviews your demo, translates your vision, and handpicks the right player.
resources.cost: $150–$225 per instrument (individual session musician tracks). Full production projects available at $2,500–$5,000+ per song.
highlights: Handpicked musicians matched to your genre
Curated studio team (not a freelancer platform)

resources.name: BeatStars
resources.description: The largest beat-selling marketplace connecting producers and artists. Browse, preview, and license beats with instant delivery. Supports exclusive and non-exclusive licenses. Recently acquired AI music startup Lemonaide (January 2026).
resources.cost: Free to browse. Beat prices set by producers (typically $20–$500+). Plans: Starter $19.99/yr (0% commission), Growth $79.99/yr, Professional $14.99/mo. 12% buyer marketplace fee on Marketplace purchases.
highlights: Largest producer community in the industry
Integrated AI music creation via Lemonaide (January 2026 acquisition)

resources.name: Airbit
resources.description: Beat marketplace focused on producer-friendly pricing. Upload and sell beats with 0% seller commission across all plans. Supports custom beat stores and flexible licensing.
resources.cost: Free Basic plan (10 beat uploads, Marketplace only). Platinum $19.99/mo or $7.99/mo billed annually (unlimited beats + custom beat store). 0% seller commission on all plans.
highlights: 0% seller commission — key differentiator vs. BeatStars

resources.name: SoundBetter — Producers
resources.description: Find and hire music producers through the SoundBetter marketplace. Filter by genre, credits, reviews, and budget. Work directly with the producer through the platform.
resources.cost: Free to browse and hire; producer rates vary (~$200–$5,000+). Clients pay no platform fee; pros pay commission or storefront subscription fee.
highlights: Same trust system as SoundBetter session musicians

resources.name: Splice — Sounds & Samples
resources.description: Massive royalty-free sample library used by 10M+ producers. Access millions of loops, one-shots, presets, and MIDI packs. Rent-to-own plugins like Serum 2. Studio collaboration platform closed March 2023.
resources.cost: Free tier available. Sounds+ $12.99/mo (100 credits), Creator $19.99/mo (200 credits), Creator+ $39.99/mo (500 credits). Rent-to-own plugins such as Serum 2 ($9.99/mo) and RC-20 ($4.99/mo).
highlights: In-DAW integration with Ableton, Studio One

resources.name: Tracklib
resources.description: Legal sample-clearance platform. Browse a catalog of real, original recordings and license samples with pre-cleared rights for your productions. Mobile app launched May 2025. Removed clearance fees for Premium/Max subscribers.
resources.cost: Free to browse and preview. Essential $5.99/mo (5 credits, no unlimited clearance), Standard $13.99/mo (15 credits), Professional $29.99/mo (35 credits), Premium $13.99+/mo (375+ credits, unlimited clearance), Max $19.99+/mo (650+ credits, unlimited clearance).
highlights: Unlimited sample clearance for Premium/Max subscribers
New Sounds section: royalty-free loops and one-shots

resources.name: SoundBetter — Mixing Engineers
resources.description: Browse and hire mixing engineers from SoundBetter's vetted roster. Filter by genre specialty, credits, reviews, and budget. Includes Grammy-winning engineers.
resources.cost: Free to browse and hire; rates set by engineers. Clients pay no platform fee; pros pay commission or storefront subscription fee.
highlights: Engineers with major label credits available

resources.name: LANDR
resources.description: AI-powered mastering platform expanded into a full production ecosystem. Includes unlimited AI mastering, distribution to streaming platforms, sample packs, 70+ plugins, and 200+ courses. Pricing restructured around bundled LANDR Studio plans.
resources.cost: LANDR Studio plans from ~$8.25/mo on annual billing up to ~$19–24/mo. Single-track pay-as-you-go available at ~$9/single. Annual plans range $23.99–$190/yr.
highlights: Unlimited free previews before you pay
Full production ecosystem (mastering, distribution, samples, plugins, courses)

resources.name: eMastered
resources.description: AI mastering service co-founded by a Grammy-winning engineer (Smith Carlson, Taylor Swift's 1989). More mastering controls than LANDR — adjust EQ, compression, stereo width, and loudness. Expanded beyond mastering to include distribution and creative tools.
resources.cost: $15/mo billed at $180/yr, $19/mo billed monthly, or $39/mo (month-to-month, cancel anytime). Includes unlimited mastering + distribution + stem separation + bonus plugins (ATOM Synth, PitchPro).
highlights: Unlimited high-res WAV masters on subscription

resources.name: AirGigs — Mixing & Mastering
resources.description: Hire mixing and mastering engineers on the AirGigs marketplace. Compare profiles, listen to before/after samples, and read reviews from other artists.
resources.cost: Service prices set by engineers. Buyers pay 4.7% fee ($5 minimum).
highlights: Wide price range for all budgets

resources.name: Fiverr — Mixing & Mastering
resources.description: Find mixing and mastering engineers on Fiverr's freelance marketplace. Good for budget-conscious projects with fast turnaround needs.
resources.cost: Services from ~$10. Fiverr Pro (vetted) engineers available at higher rates.

resources.name: BandLab — Mastering
resources.description: Free AI mastering built into the BandLab platform. Upload your finished mix and get an instant master with no watermark. Part of a free, cloud-based DAW with 60M+ users. BandLab Membership adds distribution, AI tools, and mastering controls.
resources.cost: Free (basic AI mastering). BandLab Membership ~$14.95/mo adds distribution, AI tools, and mastering intensity controls.

resources.name: SoundBetter — Singers & Songwriters
resources.description: Find and hire male and female session singers, topliners, and songwriters on SoundBetter. Filter by genre, vocal range, and budget. Includes background vocalists and topliner writers.
resources.cost: Free to browse, post jobs, and hire; vocalist rates vary (~$100–$2,000+). SoundBetter's commission is paid by the provider, not the client.

resources.name: Fiverr — Singers & Songwriters
resources.description: Hire session singers, background vocalists, jingle singers, and songwriters on Fiverr. Wide range of genres and pricing. Filter by vocal style, gender, and language.
resources.cost: Services from ~$20. Average vocal track: $50–$200+.
highlights: Huge selection of vocal styles and languages
Fiverr Pro tier of vetted vocalists

resources.name: AirGigs — Vocalists
resources.description: Hire session singers, background vocalists, and songwriters on AirGigs. Listen to audio samples, read reviews, and work through secure escrow payments.
resources.cost: Service prices set by vocalists. Buyers pay a 4.7% service fee ($5 minimum).

resources.name: Kompoz
resources.description: Online music collaboration platform for asynchronous songwriting. Upload stems, invite collaborators worldwide, and build songs together. Built-in royalty split tracking. Active as of May 2026 with 6 employees.
resources.cost: Free Starter plan. Plus $5/mo or $49/yr, Premier $10/mo or $99/yr, Pro $20/mo or $199/yr. Pricing matches original listing.
highlights: 10+ years as a leading collaboration platform
Community forums and groups by genre/instrument

resources.name: ProCollabs
resources.description: Online music collaboration platform with a manually verified membership. Share projects, find vocalists and songwriters, and collaborate across borders. ⚠️ STATUS UNCERTAIN: Very low activity as of May 2026 (1 employee listed); verify community activity before recommending.
resources.cost: Free to join (manually verified).
highlights: ⚠️ Verify current activity level — low company activity reported

resources.name: BandLab
resources.description: Free cloud-based DAW and social music platform with 60M+ users. Create, collaborate with up to 50 people per project, and share music — all from your browser or phone. Freemium ecosystem with optional paid membership.
resources.cost: Free (all core features). BandLab Membership ~$14.95/mo adds distribution, AI tools, and mastering controls.
highlights: Free multi-track recording, mixing, and mastering

resources.name: BandMix
resources.description: The largest musician classifieds site for finding local band members, session players, and music industry professionals. Search by location, instrument, genre, and experience level. Note: some users report renewal billing after cancellation — disable auto-renew when signing up.
resources.cost: Free account (limited). Premier: $14.95/mo, $37.95/3mo, or $99.95/yr ($8.33/mo).
highlights: Digital Auditions feature contacts 100 relevant musicians
Musician, Band, and Industry account types

resources.name: Soundtrap
resources.description: Cloud DAW owned by Spotify, built for real-time collaboration. Multiple users can work on the same track simultaneously with video chat. Includes loops, instruments, and podcasting tools. Pricing restructured with tiered plans.
resources.cost: Free tier available. Paid plans: Sound Starter $9.59/mo (billed yearly $115.08), Music Production $13.59/mo, Vocals & Songwriting $13.59/mo, Production & Vocals $16.59/mo.
highlights: Real-time simultaneous collaboration with video chat

resources.name: Splice — Community
resources.description: Splice's free community hub on Discord hosts beat battles, remix contests, and producer networking. Members connect, share music, collaborate, and join creative challenges; no Splice subscription needed.
resources.cost: Free (Discord community). Splice subscription from $12.99/mo for samples and tools.
highlights: Free to join — no Splice subscription required
Beat battles with major producers (Murda Beatz, Chromeo)

resources.name: ASCAP
resources.description: American Society of Composers, Authors, and Publishers. Non-profit PRO representing 20M+ musical works. Collects performance royalties from radio, TV, live venues, and streaming for songwriters and publishers.
resources.cost: Free to join as a writer. Publisher-only membership is $50 one-time. No annual dues.
highlights: Airport and hotel discounts for members
Join one PRO only — cannot also be BMI member

resources.name: BMI
resources.description: Broadcast Music, Inc. The largest US PRO, representing 1.5M+ songwriters, composers, and publishers and 25M+ musical works. Collects and distributes performance royalties for songwriters and publishers.
resources.cost: Free to join as a songwriter. No membership fee or annual dues.
highlights: Free to join — no fees for songwriters
Songwriting camps and app subscriptions for members
Good first choice for indie songwriters

resources.name: SESAC
resources.description: Selective, invitation-only PRO. Much smaller roster than ASCAP/BMI (15,000+ affiliated songwriters, composers, and publishers; 1.5M+ songs). Focus on high-profile writers in TV, film, and major releases. Unsolicited submissions not accepted.
resources.cost: Invitation only. No public fee structure.
highlights: Notable members: Adele, Bob Dylan, Neil Diamond

resources.name: SoundExchange
resources.description: Non-profit that collects digital performance royalties for sound recordings (not compositions). Covers satellite radio (SiriusXM), internet radio (Pandora non-interactive), and other non-interactive digital streams. Sole U.S. government-designated administrator for Section 114 sound recording licenses.
resources.cost: Free to register.
highlights: Collects royalties ASCAP/BMI do not cover
Pays featured artists (45%), labels (50%), and session musicians (5%)
Register even if not getting digital radio play — collects back-royalties
Does NOT cover Spotify/Apple Music interactive streams

resources.name: The MLC (Mechanical Licensing Collective)
resources.description: Non-profit created by the Music Modernization Act. Administers blanket mechanical licenses for streaming services and distributes mechanical royalties to songwriters and publishers in the US. Over $4 billion in total streaming royalties distributed.
resources.cost: Free. Fully funded by Digital Service Providers (Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon, etc.).
highlights: Collects mechanical royalties from all major streaming platforms
Search their Missing Member Lookup for unclaimed royalties

resources.name: Songtrust
resources.description: Global publishing administrator that registers your songs with 65+ collection societies across 240 countries and collects your publishing royalties. You retain 100% copyright ownership. Mechanical royalty commission increased to 20% as of January 2025.
resources.cost: One-time $100 setup fee per songwriter. Performance royalty commission: 15%. Mechanical royalty commission: 20% (as of January 2025).
highlights: No delivery obligations or advance requirements
~150K streams to break even on setup fee

resources.name: Ari's Take
resources.description: Comprehensive music business blog and podcast by Ari Herstand, author of "How to Make It in the New Music Business." Covers royalties, collaboration, sync licensing, touring, and career strategy. Blog, podcast, and newsletter all current.
resources.cost: Blog and podcast: Free. Ari's Take Academy courses: Paid (see Ari's Take Academy listing).
highlights: Praised by Forbes as "The poster child of DIY music"
Covers collaboration, splits, PROs, and sync in depth

resources.name: DIY Musician (CD Baby Blog)
resources.description: Long-running blog and podcast by CD Baby with hundreds of actionable articles on music promotion, releasing music, royalties, and career development for independent musicians. Actively publishing as of September 2026.
resources.cost: Free (blog, podcast, and newsletter).
highlights: One of the most respected indie music resources
Covers release strategies, analytics, and promotion

resources.name: Bandzoogle Blog
resources.description: Advice, inspiration, and practical resources for independent musicians. Covers marketing, website design, merchandise, revenue diversification, and music career strategies. Blog posts through 2026 confirmed.
resources.cost: Free (blog). Note: Bandzoogle website builder requires paid plan after 14-day trial (~$9.16/mo billed annually).
highlights: Practical, actionable advice for indie artists
Covers merch, marketing, and website strategy

resources.name: Soundfly
resources.description: Online music school with free and premium courses across production, songwriting, theory, and music business. Free courses include royalty collection, home recording, and touring guides. Soundfly Membership subscription available.
resources.cost: Free courses available. Soundfly Membership $12/mo or $96/yr. Friend of the Fly tier $39/mo (adds personal support and exclusive events).
highlights: Free courses on royalties, recording, and touring
Premium courses taught by Kimbra, RJD2, Kiefer
Flypaper blog with additional free articles

resources.name: Hypebot
resources.description: Daily music industry news, insights, and analysis read by 30,000+ professionals. Covers music tech, artist marketing, live music, and industry trends with a focus on independent artists. Acquired by Bandsintown in 2023.
resources.cost: Free.
highlights: Strong coverage of music tech and AI in music

resources.name: Ari's Take Academy
resources.description: Paid course platform from Ari Herstand covering royalty registration, sync licensing, touring, and release strategy. Includes community access, live Q&As, and peer feedback. Over 7,000 musicians and industry professionals enrolled.
resources.cost: Individual courses: Touring Artist $897, Special Events ~$1,297, Sync Strategies $997, Registration/Royalties/Release $997.
highlights: Step-by-step courses on royalties, sync, and touring
Community of 7,000+ musicians and industry professionals
Students often collaborate with each other

resources.name: Splice — Skills & Blog
resources.description: Free tutorials and articles on music production, sampling, and creative workflows. Skills platform offers in-depth production courses for subscribers.
resources.cost: Blog: Free. Skills tutorials included with Splice Creator plans (from $19.99/mo).

resources.name: Pibox
resources.description: Audio review and collaboration platform purpose-built for music production workflows. Leave time-stamped feedback directly on a track's waveform for organized async collaboration. Used by Universal, Sony, and Epidemic Sound. iOS app redesigned December 2025.
resources.cost: Free plan (2 users, 1 GB); Pro $10/mo ($9/mo billed annually) for unlimited projects and users.
highlights: Used by Sony, Universal, and Epidemic Sound

resources.name: Lutefish
resources.description: ⚠️ HARDWARE-REQUIRED REAL-TIME JAMMING PLATFORM — Not a pure software collaboration tool. Minnesota-based platform launched November 2024. Lutefish Stream is a plug-and-play hardware device enabling real-time audio streaming with latency as low as 30–35ms for musicians up to 500 miles apart. Backed by Wenger Corporation (80-year music manufacturing company).
resources.cost: $249 Stream device (includes 2 months of service), then $9.99/mo or $95.90/yr. Community features free without hardware.
highlights: Each remote musician needs a Lutefish Stream device + subscription
Community networking features free without hardware
New features: Individual Mix, Link Posting, Trim Audio Files (July 2025)
Sold in the US and Canada only

resources.name: CoCreatea
resources.description: Social network for musicians and other creatives, built for collaboration. Collaborate for free, build long-term producer relationships, network across 28 music roles, and work with videographers and visual artists for music videos. ⚠️ VERY NEW PLATFORM (domain registered July 12, 2025, <15 months old). Beta status with 600+ active creators.
resources.cost: Free
highlights: ⚠️ Very early stage — verify activity before recommending

resources.name: Audiomovers LISTENTO
resources.description: Collection of plugins and apps designed to stream uncompressed audio from within your DAW. Supports surround formats up to 9.1.6 Dolby Atmos on all plans, plus Apple Music spatial (binaural) rendering on Pro and above. Major update v3 released August 2025. Pro now supports 128 channels of lossless audio (up from 16). Audiomovers is now part of Abbey Road Studios.
resources.cost: Basic $12.99/mo ($99.99/yr), Pro $24.99/mo ($199.99/yr), Business $275/yr (annual only). 7-day free trial.
highlights: Pro: up to 128 channels of lossless audio (v3 upgrade from 16)
Surround sound support up to 9.1.6 Dolby Atmos
Apple Music spatial audio support (Pro tier)
New features 2025: Guest Pass, talkback, video sync
Now part of Abbey Road Studios

resources.name: TYFRA
resources.description: Music-specific professional network with full workflow integration — combining catalog storage, collaboration, DJ promotion analytics, charts, social networking, gig booking, contract/split management, and royalty invoicing in one platform. UK-based (prices in GBP).
resources.cost: Free tier; Pro £9.99/mo, Pro+ £14.99/mo.

resources.name: Sessionwire
resources.description: Real-time remote collaboration tool with bi-directional studio-quality audio (48 kHz stereo), integrated chat and HD video, file transfer, and a free DAW plugin suite (AAX, VST3, AU). Professional alternative to LISTENTO with added video/chat features built in. Pricing updated; Basic plan now starts at $9/mo.
resources.cost: Free forever (public profile, unlimited connections, guest access, free plugin suite). Basic $9/mo (host your own studio room, 1 guest, 5GB Vault). Studio $29/mo (up to 50 people, session recording, remote desktop, 100GB Vault + Puremix Pro included). Business: custom pricing. 14-day free trial (no credit card required).
highlights: Free DAW plugin suite (AAX, VST3, AU)
Studio tier ($29/mo) includes Puremix Pro ($165/yr value)

resources.name: Auxfeed
resources.description: Emerging DAW monitoring platform offering genuinely free, unlimited tier with no account required. Auxfeed Pro adds advanced metering and client listening tools. Strong alternative to Audiomovers LISTENTO for independent artists needing affordable real-time client feedback.
resources.cost: Free tier (unlimited, no account required, no watermarks). Auxfeed Pro $9.99/mo or $79/yr.
highlights: Genuinely free unlimited monitoring (no account needed)
LUFS metering, true peak analysis, loudness targets (Pro)
Affordable alternative to premium monitoring tools
Emerging platform with strong free tier

resources.name: Subvert
resources.description: Artist and label co-ownership and revenue-sharing platform. Opened to founding members November 2025 with 14,000+ artist, label, and supporter co-owners as of early 2026, ahead of public launch. Membership includes rights to vote on platform decisions and share in platform revenue.
resources.cost: Artist and label membership: Free. Supporter membership: $100 one-time fee.
highlights: Emerging platform focused on artist equity
